scope: The Continuum's bounded PASS3 speed-and-safety gate, run after the active batch sealed and before committing the remaining 249 shards to a scheduler.

added: per-stage seconds inside pack_shard (source_read, bf16_decode, fit, serialize, hash_manifest, file_write, fsync, atomic_rename, bookkeeping)
per-batch worker idle, barrier idle, and straggler cost
instrumentation.channel: PASS3_TELEMETRY.jsonl, a side channel excluded from every artifact and canonical receipt -- nondeterministic timing may never enter evidence

what_the_instrumentation_found.conclusion: Scheduler shape was worth at most ~7 percent (3.6 straggler + ~3.4 serialized fetch). The codec fit was 99.5 percent of the run. Optimizing the scheduler alone would have been optimizing the wrong thing.

root_cause.finding: pack_shard exempted every rate-overridden tensor from the ladder sampling schedule, fitting all three rungs (R0, R2, R4) and using one.
root_cause.why_the_exemption_existed: The non-survey branch fitted `production_rung` rather than the tensor's own target, so an overridden tensor had to survey every rung merely to guarantee its target got fitted at all. A correctness guard wearing a scientific justification.
root_cause.why_it_mattered_here: The frozen Math allocation overrides 56,076 of 59,585 tensors (94.1 percent). The exemption's 'uncommon case' was the whole model, so the rate survey became the pack.
root_cause.fix: Fit the tensor's own target rung directly. The sampling schedule then applies to every routed expert on equal terms; non-routed tensors (1,217 of 59,585, shape-diverse) stay exhaustively surveyed.

admissibility.why_identical_is_guaranteed: Ladder rungs share no RNG state -- _kmeans seeds its own torch.Generator per rung -- so a rung that is not fitted cannot perturb one that is.
proven_by: live: shards 30-33 packed under the new schedule match the frozen allocation's predicted payload byte-for-byte, delta 0, rung mismatches 0
admissibility.what_did_change: The survey record. Each shard header now carries ladder_survey.schedule so a reader can tell which density a given shard's survey rows were taken at; shards 1-29 were sealed under v1 and are unaltered.
admissibility.survey_science_retained: R2 and R4 relative error across routed experts have stdev 1.8e-4 and 1.0e-4 -- every routed expert is a repeat measurement of a quantity already known to four decimals. Sampling every 32nd retains the measurement and drops the repetition.

scheduler_changes_retained.independent_atomic_seal_per_shard: receipt, telemetry, eviction and progress publish on each shard's own completion
scheduler_changes_retained.immediate_work_stealing: a finished worker takes the next ready shard without waiting for its batch peers
scheduler_changes_retained.fetch_pack_overlap: producer thread keeps sources resident ahead of the pool; fetch no longer runs serially in front of an idle pool
scheduler_changes_retained.bug_found_and_fixed_in_this_change: wait(FIRST_COMPLETED) watches futures, not the queue. After one momentary queue-empty the pool held at 1 busy worker of 4. Observed live, fixed with a bounded poll used only when a slot is free and a fetch is still pending; a full pipeline costs no wakeups.

rejected.disposable_MPS_fitting_workers: not attempted. gravity_forge's MPS path has a recorded command-buffer fault on this host that silently poisoned a LATER unrelated tensor's PQ indices rather than raising at the fault. CPU is forced everywhere unattended correctness matters. A 4x deterministic CPU win was available without touching it; taking an unproven Metal win on top would trade a known-good artifact for an unbounded correctness risk.
rejected.more_workers: not attempted. MOP holds ~19 of 28 cores; the pool is already oversubscribed at 4 workers x 7 torch threads. Increasing workers blindly is forbidden by the campaign and unsupported by the measurement.

measured_before_after.workload: 4 real GLM-5.2 source shards, 213 tensors each, same host, same 4 workers x 7 torch threads
measured_before_after.contention: MOP held ~19 of 28 cores throughout BOTH arms (running 2h+ before the baseline batch and still running after), so the comparison is paired, not clean-room

after.starvation_note: an artifact of a 4-shard bounded run draining its tail with 4 workers; in a continuous 249-shard run starvation occurs only at the very end

projected_remaining.caveat: projection at current MOP contention; an idle box would be faster and a heavier MOP slower

not_evidence_of: output divergence, capability, or end-to-end behaviour
